rationale: Eubacterium rectale ferments acetate and arginine as primary C and N sources, producing butyrate as the dominant product. Acetate (12 mmol/gDW/h) drives butyrate synthesis; arginine (4 mmol/gDW/h) provides both C and N via dihydrolase pathway. Amino acids supplement C and N. Growth rate of 0.45 /h is supported by ~50 mmol C/gDW/h input, with 14.85 mmol consumed for biomass, remainder as fermentation products (butyrate, acetate, CO₂, formate). Nitrogen balance: arginine + amino acids + trace NH₄ supply 7.5 mmol N/gDW/h; growth consumes 3.15, excess released as NH₃.
